note: Oral gepants for acute migraine (members BI 44370, MK-3207, rimegepant, ubrogepant), developed in primates because rodent CGRP receptors bind gepants poorly; MK-3207 worked but was dropped for liver signals, ubrogepant and rimegepant were approved.
label: Migraine (gepants)

engagement.note: MK-3207 blocked capsaicin-evoked, CGRP-mediated forearm skin vasodilation in rhesus monkeys at 0.8 nM (50%) and 7 nM (90%) plasma.
engagement.quote: MK-3207 produced a concentration-dependent inhibition of dermal vasodilation, with plasma concentrations of 0.8 and 7 nM required to block 50 and 90% of the blood flow increase, respectively.
engagement.judgement: Primate assay because gepants bind rodent receptors weakly. The rhesus CIDV assay itself dates from Hershey 2005 (doi 10.1016/j.regpep.2004.10.010, a non-member compound), hence model_first_use_year 2005. model_filed=true: FDA's 2019 ubrogepant pharmacology review names capsaicin-induced dermal vasodilation in monkey among its 'animal efficacy models'.

engagement.note: In healthy volunteers MK-3207 blocked capsaicin skin vasodilation with EC50 ~1.6 nM and EC90 14 nM, twofold the rhesus 0.8 and 7 nM.
engagement.quote: Results suggest that MK-3207 is a potent compound (EC50 of ∼1.6 nM) and that the majority of the exposure−response relationship occurs at low nM concentration range
engagement.confidence_note: Open-access full text read (PMC4415719). The journal renders 'EC 50' and 'n m' in small caps; normalised to EC50 and nM in the quote.
engagement.reason: Human CIDV potency within 2x of rhesus
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Li 2015 says the assay was 'first established and validated in the rhesus monkey' but does not print the rhesus MK-3207 numbers, so comparison_stated=false with Salvatore 2010 as model_src. The ratio is 1.99x (EC50) and 2.0x (EC90), on the edge of within_2x. Moore 2020 (doi 10.1124/jpet.119.261065, abstract) later states the comparison in one source for ubrogepant: CIDV EC50 3.2 nM rhesus vs 2.6 nM human; that would be a same-status entry on the same model, so it is recorded here rather than as an entry. readout_tier direct: in vivo blockade of an evoked CGRP stimulus.
engagement.magnitude_basis: plasma EC50 / EC90 for CIDV inhibition, human vs rhesus (1.6 vs 0.8 nM; 14 vs 7 nM)

dose.model: Rhesus CIDV exposure target, translated to human CIDV PK/PD
dose.note: The class set its dose target as the plasma level giving 90% CIDV block; for MK-3207 rhesus put it at 7 nM.
dose.quote: MK-3207 produced a concentration-dependent inhibition of dermal vasodilation, with plasma concentrations of 0.8 and 7 nM required to block 50 and 90% of the blood flow increase, respectively.
dose.judgement: The EC90-for-2-h target was anchored on telcagepant (not a member) and applied to MK-3207 through a healthy-volunteer CIDV study; the model is the CIDV EC90 target as a whole, rhesus-derived and human-calibrated.

dose.model: Rhesus CIDV exposure target, translated to human CIDV PK/PD
dose.note: CIDV predicted MK-3207 efficacy from 20 mg with a plateau at 40-100 mg; the phase 2 added 200 mg for insufficient efficacy at 20-100 mg, and only 200 mg was clearly significant.
dose.quote: Among the tested doses, the pairwise difference vs. placebo for 2 h pain freedom was significant for 200 mg (P < 0.001) and nominally significant for 10 mg and 100 mg (P < 0.05).
dose.confidence_note: Open-access full text read. The authors themselves call it a 'reasonable correlation'; the contra is my reading of the trial data.
dose.judgement: Prospective: Li 2015 says the CIDV predictions 'provided a quantitative rationale for dose selection in a phase 2 clinical trial of MK-3207'. Hewitt 2011 (doi 10.1177/0333102411398399; NCT00712725, results posted 2010-11-22) reports 'a 200 mg dose was added due to insufficient efficacy at the top three (20, 50, 100 mg) doses', and only 200 mg was significant pairwise on the primary endpoint. That is the brief's 'reached, failed, a higher dose worked' row: dose contra, not derived_from efficacy since the drug did work. The authors (Merck) call it a reasonable correlation and note overlapping CIs from 10 mg up, so source_calls_it=match against my contra; judged on the data per decision 13. Ubrogepant and rimegepant tolerability margins (decision 16) were not added here: they score the toxic end with a different model and would turn this efficacy-end miss back by model_change, which I judged wrong.
dose.magnitude_basis: dose with clear 2-h pain freedom (200 mg) vs predicted plateau 40-100 mg (10x vs the 20 mg target)

dose.note: Ubrogepant blocked CGRP relaxation of human isolated meningeal, cerebral and coronary arteries; potency was set beside clinical plasma levels only later.
dose.quote: In intracranial arteries, both blockers antagonized the calcitonin gene-related peptide-induced relaxations more potently when compared to the inhibition observed in distal human coronary arteries, with atogepant showing a higher potency.
dose.judgement: Opening entry at the first published use of this system for a member (ubrogepant). The study was already in the ubrogepant NDA (FDA PharmR lists ex vivo vasoactivity in human arteries), so model_filed true.
dose.model: Human isolated coronary, cerebral and middle meningeal arteries (ex vivo CGRP relaxation and vasoconstriction)

dose.magnitude_basis: free Cmax at approved dose vs ex vivo concentration that shifts the CGRP relaxation curve
dose.confidence_note: Abstract plus full-text Table 1 (rimegepant 75 mg free Cmax vs calculated pEC50 shift); ubrogepant row not read in detail.
dose.note: Set beside published clinical Cmax and protein binding, every gepant's free plasma level at its approved dose inhibited CGRP relaxation of human meningeal arteries.
dose.short: Approved doses reach ex vivo blocking levels
dose.quote: We also showed that all gepants are effective at inhibiting functional responses to CGRP at their therapeutic plasma concentrations.
dose.judgement: Retrodiction: the ex vivo potency was connected to doses already shown effective and approved (ubrogepant 2019, rimegepant 2020), so retro, not same. The comparison is stated by the paper, which combines clinical PK with its own artery data.
dose.model: Human isolated coronary, cerebral and middle meningeal arteries (ex vivo CGRP relaxation and vasoconstriction)

efficacy.note: With rodents uninformative, the gepants' in vivo efficacy model was primate CGRP-driven skin or facial blood flow; MK-3207 blocked it in rhesus.
efficacy.quote: As a consequence of species selectivity, the in vivo potency was assessed in a rhesus monkey pharmacodynamic assay measuring capsaicin-induced changes in forearm dermal blood flow via laser Doppler imaging.
efficacy.judgement: The same primate vascular readout serves engagement and efficacy; FDA's ubrogepant review calls it an 'animal efficacy model'. Rimegepant's discovery paper used the related primate CGRP-induced facial blood flow model (Luo 2012, doi 10.1021/jm3013147, abstract). No preclinical model was found published for BI 44370.

efficacy.note: MK-3207 met its primary endpoint, a positive dose-response for 2-h pain freedom in 547 patients; every later member also met its primary endpoint.
efficacy.quote: A positive dose-response trend was demonstrated when data were combined across all MK-3207 doses for two-hour pain freedom (p < .001).
efficacy.reason: Every member met its primary endpoint
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me (Hewitt does not set the rhesus data beside the trial in the abstract). Year 2010 from the registry results posting of NCT00712725 (2010-11-22), before the 2011 epub. The dose miss is counted once, in dose. No member failed on efficacy, so neg is unavailable.

patient_trials.quote: Efficacy of BI 44370 TA was shown in a dose-dependent manner in the treatment of acute migraine attacks.
In Study MD-02, the 50 mg ubrogepant dose was also statistically superior to placebo on both co-primary endpoints
75 mg was effective and demonstrated statistically significant superior results on both co-primary endpoints compared to placebo.

efficacy.note: Oral ubrogepant reversed stress- and NO-donor-evoked cephalic allodynia in primed rats (ED50 ~50 mg/kg), a year after its phase 3 wins.
efficacy.quote: Both ubrogepant and sumatriptan demonstrated efficacy as acute medications for stress- and nitric oxide donor-evoked cephalic allodynia in a preclinical model of medication overuse headache, consistent with their clinical efficacy in the acute treatment of migraine.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction: run after ubrogepant's phase 3 results and approval (the paper says it 'was recently approved'), so retro. Comparison stated in the conclusion.
efficacy.model: Rat sumatriptan-primed two-hit medication-overuse headache model (stress / NO-donor allodynia)

efficacy.confidence_note: Paywalled; abstract only. Species of the facial blood flow model not named in the abstract (likely marmoset).
efficacy.note: Rimegepant's discovery paper rested its in vivo efficacy on dose-dependent block of CGRP-induced facial blood flow in a primate.
efficacy.quote: Compound 8 has good oral bioavailability in rat and cynomolgus monkey, attractive overall preclinical properties, and shows dose-dependent activity in a primate model of CGRP-induced facial blood flow.
efficacy.judgement: Distinct from the draft's rhesus CIDV (exogenous CGRP, facial blood flow, rimegepant's own program), though the draft's efficacy note mentions 'facial blood flow' in passing.
efficacy.model: Primate CGRP-induced facial blood flow (rimegepant / BMS-927711)

efficacy.note: In 885 patients, rimegepant 75, 150 and 300 mg beat placebo on the primary endpoint, 2-h pain freedom.
efficacy.quote: BMS-927711 is superior to placebo at several different doses (75 mg, 150 mg, and 300 mg) and has an excellent tolerability profile.
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me: Marcus cites 'in vivo efficacy without vasoconstrictor effect' but does not show the primate data. Year is the 2013 epub; NCT01430442 results posted 2020-09-03.
efficacy.model: Primate CGRP-induced facial blood flow (rimegepant / BMS-927711)

safety.model: Rat and rhesus toxicology (MK-3207; not published or filed)
safety.note: Merck dropped MK-3207 after delayed liver-test abnormalities in extended phase 1 studies; its animal toxicology was never published, so no comparison exists.
safety.quote: some subjects in extended Phase I clinical pharmacology studies were found to have experienced delayed, asymptomatic liver test abnormalities, generally following discontinuation of drug administration.
safety.confidence_note: Merck press release of 2009-09-10 as reproduced by Fierce Biotech.
safety.judgement: Under the brief this could be a contra on the animal battery's silence, but no source documents what MK-3207's rat or monkey studies showed, so left untested rather than stretched.

safety.model: In vitro hepatotoxicity assays plus DILIsym simulation
safety.note: Hepatocyte assays fed into DILIsym predicted no ALT rises for ubrogepant; an 8-week intermittent-dosing study and the trial database showed no hepatic signal.
safety.quote: In the 8-week hepatic safety study described above, there were no differences in elevations of transaminase between placebo patients and those that received 100 mg ubrogepant (refer to Table 9).
safety.confidence_note: FDA summary and pharmacology reviews of NDA 211765 read in the source bundle text.
safety.judgement: Model side: FDA pharmacology review (Reference ID 4535571) quotes the sponsor that 'no ALT elevations were predicted for any of the protocols tested'. Smith 2020 (doi 10.1093/toxsci/kfaa093) states the comparison and calls it 'the first published example of DILIsym predicting liver safety of a dosing regimen before the clinical trial'. The same paper reports DILIsym 'successfully modeled liver toxicity for telcagepant and MK-3207', a retrodiction for member MK-3207 published in 2020; recording it as a later retro entry would show this prospective match as a retrodiction, so it is kept here. Woodhead 2022 (doi 10.1093/toxsci/kfac051) extends the prospective clean call to rimegepant. Rimegepant's rat liver vacuolation/necrosis and monkey hemolysis came only at exposures FDA called substantially above the 75 mg dose, and no hepatic signal appeared in patients. The 8-week hepatic study is not registered; registry_date is the ubrogepant long-term safety study NCT02873221.
safety.magnitude_basis: proportion with ALT > 3x ULN, predicted 0% vs observed no excess over placebo

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; the FDA PharmR for NDA 211765 states the same result (no constriction up to 100 µM).
safety.note: Ubrogepant, up to 100 µM, did not constrict human coronary arteries ex vivo, unlike zolmitriptan; rimegepant was likewise non-constrictive in its NDA.
safety.quote: Neither of the gepants had vasoconstrictor effect at any of the concentrations studied in human coronary arteries, whereas zolmitriptan elicited concentration-dependent contractions.
safety.judgement: The class's vascular-safety model. FDA summary review (2019) set the ex vivo result beside trials that excluded major CV disease and called the data insufficient to establish CV safety, which is not yet a comparison.
safety.model: Human isolated coronary, cerebral and middle meningeal arteries (ex vivo CGRP relaxation and vasoconstriction)

safety.magnitude_basis: change in arterial circumference after dosing (predicted none, observed none)
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (Europe PMC). Small single-centre study (n=15); MMA is the smallest vessel imaged. Lusk 2026 found no MI excess for abortive gepants (aHR 1.16, 95% CI 0.85-1.57).
safety.reason: No vasoconstriction, as predicted ex vivo
safety.note: During spontaneous attacks in 15 women, rimegepant 75 mg did not constrict cerebral or meningeal arteries on MR angiography, as predicted ex vivo.
safety.quote: Rimegepant did not induce measurable constriction of cerebral or meningeal arteries during spontaneous migraine attacks.
safety.judgement: Paired by me: Chaudhry opens with 'Preclinical studies have reported no direct vascular effects of CGRP antagonists' but does not set the ex vivo data beside its own, so comparison_stated false. Model side for rimegepant is the FDA summary review, 'no vasoconstrictive effects on isolated human coronary or cerebral arteries'. The ischemic-stroke association in Lusk 2026 is a different harm (collateral flow, not constriction) and is scored on the mouse MCAO track. Registered NCT06470958; no results posting checked.
safety.model: Human isolated coronary, cerebral and middle meningeal arteries (ex vivo CGRP relaxation and vasoconstriction)

safety.note: Rimegepant pretreatment enlarged infarcts after brief MCA occlusion in mice and high doses raised mortality; the authors predicted worse coincidental ischemic events in patients.
safety.short: Gepants worsen ischemic stroke in mice
safety.quote: Rimegepant 10mg/kg increased infarct volumes by 60% after 20-minute ischemia (p = 0.03); 100mg/kg caused 75% mortality after 60-minute occlusion.
safety.judgement: Rimegepant is a member, so product_in_model true; olcegepant (not a member) was the main drug in the paper.
safety.model: Mouse transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (gepant pretreatment)

safety.magnitude_basis: ischemic stroke risk with gepant exposure (mouse infarct +60% vs human aHR 1.36)
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC12782279). Observational claims study; initiators had more baseline CV morbidity; the abortive group includes zavegepant (not a member); the mouse model predicts severity given ischemia, the cohort measures coded stroke incidence.
safety.reason: Patients showed the predicted stroke excess
safety.note: In US claims, starting an abortive gepant carried a higher ischemic stroke hazard (aHR 1.36), the harm the mouse model predicted.
safety.quote: Similarly, abortive small molecule CGRP inhibitor initiation was associated with a higher hazard of ischemic stroke (aHR 1.36 [95% CI: 1.12 – 1.64])
safety.judgement: Paired by me: Lusk does not cite the mouse data. Direction matches (CGRP-receptor blockade aggravates cerebral ischemia), but endpoint differs (infarct size/risk after occlusion vs stroke incidence), hence low confidence. Not a trial, so no registry date. Quote is the opening of a longer sentence.
safety.model: Mouse transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (gepant pretreatment)

safety.magnitude_basis: dose boundary for DILI risk (predicted >300 mg/day vs clinical 1% at ≤100 mg, 42% at >500 mg)
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC7553701). The paper does not date the MK-3207 BA-LRA run; the assay was built after MK-3207's 2009 discontinuation, so treated as retrodiction.
safety.note: A rat liver signature put MK-3207's DILI risk above ~300 mg/day; in phase 2, ALT >3x ULN hit 1% at ≤100 mg, 42% above 500 mg.
safety.short: Rat signature reproduces MK-3207 liver injury
safety.quote: In the rat BA-LRA study, a median signature score of 0.34 was achieved predicting a lower clinical risk for DILI at projected clinical doses of < 200 mg, but more significant risk at daily doses > 300 mg.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction: MK-3207's liver signal (Merck 2009) was known before this assay existed, so retro, not same. The same paper sets the clinical ALT rates beside the score, so comparison_stated true. Different system from the draft's DILIsym track and its conventional GLP toxicology track (which the same table shows missed the signal).
safety.model: Rat in vivo liver bioactivation transcriptional response assay (BA-LRA)

safety.magnitude_basis: hazard flag (positive) vs clinical ALT elevations
safety.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC7553701); the HepatoPac method paper (Kang 2020) not read. No dose quantitation, so hazard identification only.
safety.note: MK-3207 drove the reactive-metabolite gene response in rat HepatoPac cultures well past the assay's positive threshold, matching its clinical liver injury.
safety.quote: dose-dependent increases in the transcriptional response to CRM responsive genes were observed, well exceeding the positive threshold of the assay.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction run after MK-3207's 2009 liver signal. Separate from the in vivo BA-LRA track because it is an in vitro culture system (model_kind ex_vivo is the nearest enum).
safety.model: Rat HepatoPac micropatterned hepatocyte co-culture, reactive-metabolite transcriptional response

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. FDA summary reviews (2019, 2020) state no MOH data exist for the class.
safety.note: Repeated ubrogepant did not prime rats for medication-overuse headache, unlike sumatriptan; no patient MOH study of a member was found to compare.
safety.short: No MOH predicted; untested in patients
safety.quote: Unlike sumatriptan, ubrogepant 100 mg/kg in repeated effective doses did not produce cutaneous allodynia or latent sensitization.
safety.judgement: Prospective prediction (no clinical MOH data in 2020). Only reviews assert gepants do not cause MOH; none is an admissible source.
safety.model: Rat sumatriptan-primed two-hit medication-overuse headache model (stress / NO-donor allodynia)
Rat, mouse and monkey GLP toxicology (MK-3207)
safety.note: Monroe 2020 publishes MK-3207's chronic rat (30x), mouse (14x) and monkey (4x) studies with no liver signal, beside phase 2 ALT>3x ULN and a Hy's law case.
safety.short: Animal tox silent on MK-3207 liver injury
safety.quote: No liver safety signals of concern were noted
safety.confidence_note: Full text PMC7553701 Table 1 and text; a 1-month dog study at 17x showed slight periportal vacuolation attributed to weight loss (rule question).
safety.judgement: Comparison stated by the source; the animal studies ran before the clinical signal, so contra rather than retro. Added from the models checker's verified lead.
safety.reason: Animal toxicology silent; patients showed liver injury
